hero.headline: Oil prices jump and global stocks fall after Iran and Israel exchange strikes
hero.body:
Oil prices surged and global stock markets experienced sharp declines after Iran and Israel launched attacks against each other, threatening the stability of a fragile ceasefire that had been in place since early April. The renewed hostilities triggered immediate volatility across financial markets as investors reassessed the risks of further escalation in the Middle East.

Technology stocks suffered the most significant losses in Asian trading. Markets in South Korea and Japan were hit particularly hard, with the Kospi soaring 7.5% and the Nikkei 225 gaining more than 5% in earlier trading before reversing course. The sudden reversal highlighted how quickly geopolitical tensions can derail market momentum, as investors fled from riskier assets amid uncertainty about the conflict's trajectory.

The spike in oil prices reflected traders' immediate concerns about potential disruptions to energy supplies. Brent crude oil and US crude futures both climbed as markets priced in the possibility that escalating hostilities could threaten production or disrupt transportation through the strategically critical Strait of Hormuz. The price movements underscored how sensitive global energy markets remain to conflicts in major oil-producing regions.

According to Kathleen Brooks, a research director at XTB, markets will closely monitor whether the ceasefire holds. "Only if the US or Iran walk away from the ceasefire completely and bombing restarts do we see the oil price potentially surging back to the highs of this week above $110 per barrel for Brent crude, which could also cause stocks and bonds to slump," she said.

The market reaction demonstrated how quickly geopolitical events in one region ripple through financial systems worldwide. Military exchanges between two countries rapidly affected stock exchanges across Asia and beyond, influencing everything from technology companies to energy contracts traded globally.

Jim Reid, a markets strategist at Deutsche Bank, noted the uncertainty ahead. "Investors will be breathing a big sigh of relief that an off-ramp out of the war is being taken even as there'll be various elements to watch to see whether this leads to sustained de-escalation," he said. Key questions remained about whether the ceasefire would hold, whether it would extend to Israel's actions in Lebanon, and whether talks could lead to a permanent end to hostilities.

The renewed hostilities cast doubt on the durability of diplomatic efforts to stabilize the region. Market participants now face the challenge of assessing whether the attacks represent a temporary escalation or the beginning of a broader conflict that could sustain elevated oil prices and continued pressure on risk assets. The uncertainty is expected to keep markets volatile until the situation becomes clearer.

cards.headline: At least 19 killed as magnitude-7.8 earthquake strikes southern Philippines
cards.teaser: A powerful earthquake in the southern Philippines triggered small tsunami waves and left at least 19 people dead.
cards.body:
A magnitude-7.8 earthquake struck the southern Philippines early Monday, killing at least 19 people and injuring more than 200 others. The powerful quake collapsed buildings across the region, prompting rescue operations as authorities worked to assess the full extent of damage.

The earthquake generated a 3-foot tsunami that affected nearby coasts in the Philippines, Indonesia, and Japan. Residents were warned to avoid damaged buildings and structures due to the risk of aftershocks following the major seismic event.

cards.headline: At least 12 injured in shooting at Toledo street festival, suspects at large
cards.body:
At least 12 people were shot near the Old West End Festival in Toledo, Ohio on Saturday evening, with police continuing to search for at least two suspects who officers believe were firing at each other.

The gunfire erupted just after 5:30 p.m. near the historic neighborhood festival, which features live music and architectural home tours. The shooting sent attendees into chaos as gunfire broke out in the area.

Toledo police deputy chief Joseph Heffernan said the shooters were "probably shooting at each other" when the violence occurred. Two of the victims were reported to be in critical condition, according to police.

Festival organizers cancelled planned events scheduled for Sunday as the investigation continued into the second day. Law enforcement responded quickly to the scene and transported victims for medical treatment.

Witnesses described scenes of panic as festival-goers fled the area after shots were fired. The Old West End Festival is an annual community event held in one of Toledo's historic districts, typically drawing large crowds to the neighborhood known for its Victorian-era homes.

The exact number of shooters and the circumstances leading to the violence remain under investigation as police work to identify and locate the suspects. Authorities have not released information about potential motives or whether the incident involved targeted individuals.

The shooting represents the latest incident of gun violence at a public gathering in the United States. Mass shootings at community events have become an increasing concern for law enforcement agencies tasked with securing large outdoor festivals and gatherings. Toledo police have urged anyone with information about the shooting to come forward to help apprehend those responsible.

Police presence in the area has been increased as investigators review witness accounts and any available surveillance footage. The incident adds to a growing number of shootings at public events across the country, raising questions about security measures at community festivals.

Toledo officials have not yet announced whether future events in the area will see enhanced security protocols as the search for the suspects continues. The investigation remains active as authorities work to piece together the events that led to the violence at the popular community gathering.

cards.headline: Treasury plans to use Iranian assets for Gulf reconstruction
cards.teaser: The Treasury Department intends to redirect frozen Iranian assets to help Gulf allies rebuild damage from the war, according to a report citing sources familiar with the secretary's thinking.
cards.body:
The Treasury Department plans to use Iranian assets to assist Gulf allies in rebuilding after damage sustained during the war with Iran, CBS News reported. A source aware of Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's thinking said the department intends to redirect the frozen assets for reconstruction efforts in Gulf nations.

The move would represent a significant use of Iranian financial holdings to compensate countries affected by Iranian military actions. The United States has maintained frozen Iranian assets for years, and their potential use for allied reconstruction marks a shift in how those funds might be deployed.

cards.headline: Trump's intelligence pick scuttles bipartisan deal on surveillance powers
cards.body:
President Trump's decision to appoint Bill Pulte as director of national intelligence has derailed congressional efforts to secure a long-term extension of Section 702 surveillance authorities. The move has upended what appeared to be a bipartisan agreement on renewing the controversial spy powers.

Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act allows intelligence agencies to collect communications of foreign targets operating outside the country without a warrant. The provision has sparked intense debate between national security officials who argue it remains essential for counterterrorism operations and civil liberties advocates concerned about potential government overreach.

A procedural vote in the Senate on Friday underscored the political damage caused by Pulte's appointment. Seven Republican senators joined all Democrats to block the extension measure in a 47-52 vote. Senate Majority Leader John Thune acknowledged the chamber would attempt another vote the following week but expressed limited confidence it would succeed.

Pulte, a major Republican donor and heir to a home construction fortune, has no previous experience in intelligence work. He currently leads the Federal Housing Finance Agency and has overseen Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. Democrats and some Republicans have raised serious concerns about his appointment. Mark Warner, the Senate Intelligence Committee vice-chair, told NPR that Pulte was selected solely for his loyalty to Trump and that his lack of intelligence, law enforcement, or congressional experience would essentially "disarm" the country against adversaries including Russia, China, and Iran.

Warner personally asked Senate leadership to convince Trump to reverse the appointment, with Democratic sources indicating that a bipartisan surveillance deal could collapse without such intervention. Republican concerns also centered on Trump's use of Pulte to challenge Trump's political opponents, with Senator Thune warning that a "weaponized" national intelligence director would face significant obstacles to permanent confirmation.

Trump has compounded these concerns by instructing Pulte to begin firing personnel at the intelligence office. Speaking to the Wall Street Journal, Trump said the director of national intelligence position is "unnecessary and/or too big" and wants it reduced. He told Pulte he is "less shackled" in his temporary role, suggesting this status gives him more power to take drastic action during his limited time in the position.

The surveillance program is set to expire next week. An earlier attempt to extend Section 702 for 18 months failed in the House last month after 20 Republican representatives rebelled against the measure, leading to a compromise 45-day negotiation period.

The uncertainty surrounding Section 702's future comes as Trump has also suggested using his intelligence apparatus to investigate unsubstantiated claims about election fraud, raising additional questions about the direction of the intelligence community under his administration.

cards.headline: OPEC Plus to increase oil production despite Strait of Hormuz concerns
cards.teaser: The oil cartel plans to boost output by 188,000 barrels per day even as vast amounts of oil remain stranded by disruptions to the key shipping route.
cards.body:
OPEC Plus announced plans to increase oil production by 188,000 barrels per day, a move analysts described as largely symbolic given current shipping constraints. The decision comes as the cease-fire in Iran remains uncertain, creating ongoing volatility in global energy markets.

The planned production increase faces practical limitations due to the effective shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz, which has left substantial quantities of oil unable to reach global markets. The cartel's announcement appeared aimed at signaling its commitment to supply stability even as the strategic waterway remains compromised by regional tensions.

hero.headline: Earthquake in Southern Philippines Kills at Least 15
hero.teaser: A 7.8-magnitude earthquake struck off the island of Mindanao, toppling buildings and damaging bridges.
hero.body:
A magnitude-7.8 earthquake struck off the coast of Mindanao in the southern Philippines early Monday, killing at least 19 people and injuring more than 200 others. The powerful quake collapsed buildings across the region and triggered a 3-foot tsunami that reached nearby coasts.

Rescue operations continued as authorities warned residents to avoid damaged structures due to the risk of aftershocks. Police officials reported that many buildings sustained significant damage, though a full assessment was hampered by ongoing rescue efforts in affected areas.

cards.headline: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan Wins Re-election
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan secured a mandate to continue peace talks brokered by President Trump despite pressure from Moscow.
cards.body:
Armenia's ruling pro-Europe party has won parliamentary elections, strengthening Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan's pivot toward Europe and away from Russia. Pashinyan's Civil Contract party secured a slim majority in the South Caucasus country, while the opposition Strong Armenia alliance, backed by Russian-Armenian billionaire Samvel Karapetyan, won 25% of parliament's seats.

The election result confirms Armenia's shift in foreign policy orientation despite warnings from Moscow. Pashinyan can now continue pursuing deeper integration with Europe and advance peace negotiations in the region.

cards.headline: Chinese President Xi Jinping Visits North Korea
cards.teaser: Beijing is attempting to reassert influence over North Korea as a strategically vital partner.
cards.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping traveled to North Korea for a two-day visit, his first in nearly seven years. The trip aims to revitalize China's relationship with its only formal treaty ally, as Beijing seeks to reassert influence over the strategically important country.

The China-North Korea relationship has faced strain in recent years due to a sharp decline in trade during the Covid-19 pandemic and Pyongyang's growing ties with Russia. Xi is expected to meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un in Pyongyang as part of efforts to strengthen the partnership.

cards.headline: Asian Tech Stocks Fall After Middle East Attacks Resume
cards.teaser: Markets in South Korea and Japan saw technology stocks sell off as oil prices rose following renewed Iran-Israel strikes.
cards.body:
Technology stocks declined sharply across Asian markets on Monday, with South Korea and Japan experiencing significant sell-offs. The declines followed a sharp drop in U.S. tech stocks the previous week, as investors grew concerned about the spending requirements for companies leading the artificial intelligence boom.

The market turmoil coincided with renewed military attacks between Iran and Israel, which sparked fears of regional instability. Oil prices climbed as traders worried about potential supply disruptions from the Middle East conflict. The combination reflected broader investor anxiety about both the sustainability of tech valuations and geopolitical risks.

cards.headline: North Korea's Economy Strengthens Under Kim Jong-un
cards.teaser: Kim Jong-un used the pandemic to tighten control and energized the economy by leveraging Russia's war in Ukraine.
cards.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping visited North Korea for the first time in nearly seven years, seeking to revitalize China's relationship with its formal treaty ally. Trade between the two countries had virtually frozen during the Covid-19 pandemic.

North Korea's relationship with Russia has grown increasingly close in recent years, straining its traditionally central ties with China. Kim Jong-un leveraged the pandemic to tighten control domestically while simultaneously pursuing new economic opportunities through alignment with Russia amid international sanctions over its invasion of Ukraine.

cards.headline: Extreme Heat Strains Communities in Pakistan
cards.teaser: Residents of Dadu District face 125-degree temperatures in an area prone to sandstorms, drought, and flooding.
cards.body:
Communities in Dadu District, Pakistan, are enduring extreme heat with temperatures reaching 125 degrees Fahrenheit. Residents are searching for shade and relief in a region that faces multiple environmental challenges throughout the year. The district is prone to sandstorms, drought, and flooding, with each season bringing different hardships.

The extreme temperatures add to the ongoing struggles of people living in the area, who must cope with rapidly shifting environmental conditions. The heat compounds existing vulnerabilities in a region already dealing with water scarcity and agricultural challenges.

cards.headline: Great White Shark Filmed in Mediterranean Sea
cards.teaser: A volunteer diver captured rare footage of an endangered Great White shark between Tunisia and Sicily.
cards.body:
A volunteer diver captured rare footage of an endangered Great White shark swimming in the Mediterranean Sea between Tunisia and Sicily. The diver experienced visible emotion during the encounter, describing himself as shaking while filming the protected species.

Great White sharks are rarely spotted in Mediterranean waters, making this documented sighting particularly noteworthy. The footage provides researchers with valuable evidence of the species' presence in European waters and contributes to scientific understanding of these sharks in the region.

cards.headline: Father and twin 10-year-old boys found dead in Canoga Park shooting
cards.teaser: Police in Los Angeles are investigating an apparent murder-suicide that left a father and his twin 10-year-old sons dead in Canoga Park.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Police Department responded to a shooting in Canoga Park that left three people dead. Officers found a father and his twin 10-year-old sons at the scene. Police are investigating the incident as an apparent murder-suicide.

The shooting took place in the Canoga Park neighborhood of Los Angeles.

cards.headline: Iran releases video of missile strikes on Israel, promises week of attacks
cards.teaser: Iran published footage of missiles it launched at Israel and said the strikes mark the start of a week of continuous attacks.
cards.body:
Iran released footage of missiles being launched at Israel, describing the strikes as the beginning of a full week of continuous attacks. The video was distributed as part of Iran's public messaging about its military operations.

The exchange of fire between Iran and Israel early Monday represented a significant escalation in their conflict. Yemen's Houthi rebels also warned they would target Israel-affiliated ships in the Red Sea, raising concerns that the confrontation could expand into a broader regional war.

cards.headline: Danish footballer Christian Eriksen in good spirits after on-field collapse
cards.teaser: Denmark midfielder Christian Eriksen is expected to be discharged from the hospital soon after collapsing during a match against Ukraine.
cards.body:
Christian Eriksen is in good spirits following his collapse during Denmark's Euro 2020 match against Ukraine, according to the national team's doctor Morten Boesen. The midfielder is expected to be discharged from hospital soon.

Eriksen collapsed on the pitch during the game, requiring immediate medical intervention. Boesen's update on his condition has provided reassurance to fans and the football community following the alarming incident.

cards.headline: Chinese President Xi Jinping visits North Korea
cards.teaser: Xi Jinping traveled to North Korea as Beijing seeks to reassert influence over its strategically important but unpredictable partner.
cards.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping visited North Korea for the first time in nearly seven years, with plans to meet leader Kim Jong-un in Pyongyang for a two-day trip. The visit signals Beijing's effort to revitalize ties with its only formal treaty ally.

The China-North Korea relationship has weakened in recent years due to a sharp decline in trade during the pandemic and Pyongyang's strengthening ties with Russia. Xi's trip represents an attempt to reassert Chinese influence over the strategically important nation.

cards.headline: Government to release guidance on children's screen time
cards.teaser: Ministers plan to issue recommendations on how much time children between ages five and 16 should spend on screens.
cards.body:
Ministers are issuing guidance on children's screen use, with recommendations tailored for those aged five to 16. The guidance will include advice on appropriate amounts of screen time for each age group.

The move reflects mounting concerns about how digital device use affects children's development and wellbeing. Officials have developed these recommendations to give families clear direction when making decisions about technology use.

cards.headline: Asian tech stocks plunge after record rally
cards.teaser: Markets in South Korea and Japan sold off sharply as investors dumped technology stocks that had been leading a prolonged rally.
cards.body:
Technology stocks across Asia experienced a sharp sell-off, with markets in South Korea and Japan hit particularly hard. The decline followed a record rally that had pushed valuations higher, prompting investors to take profits.

The downturn was intensified by renewed military attacks between Iran and Israel, which sparked a broader retreat from riskier assets. Oil prices rose amid the escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.

cards.headline: Airlines face $100 billion additional fuel costs as oil prices climb
cards.teaser: Global airlines expect significantly higher jet fuel bills this year, with the industry warning that fare increases are inevitable.
cards.body:
Airlines worldwide are bracing for an additional $100 billion in fuel costs this year as oil prices surge due to conflict-related supply concerns. Industry executives warned that the sharp increase in operating costs will force carriers to raise ticket prices for passengers.

The International Air Transport Association addressed the fuel cost shock at its annual meeting in Rio, where airline CEOs also criticized engine makers for pricing practices. The industry slashed its profit forecast for 2026 as the energy price spike threatens to undermine what had been expected to be a strong recovery year for global air travel.

cards.headline: Europe unveils plans to reduce dependence on American technology
cards.teaser: European officials announced a technology sovereignty package aimed at decreasing reliance on U.S. tech companies and infrastructure.
cards.body:
The European Union introduced a comprehensive package of measures designed to build technological independence from American companies. Officials expressed concerns about overreliance on U.S. technology infrastructure, with one stating that Europe wants to ensure nobody has a kill switch over its digital systems.

The initiative includes support for strategic technology projects and encouragement of European alternatives to American platforms and services. ASML's CEO responded to the announcement by suggesting the EU Commission should not try to direct strategic projects, highlighting tensions between government ambitions and industry preferences on how to achieve tech sovereignty.

cards.headline: Dollar reaches two-month high as Federal Reserve rate hike expectations grow
cards.teaser: The U.S. dollar climbed to its strongest level in two months as investors increased bets on further interest rate increases.
cards.body:
The dollar rose to a two-month peak as market participants ramped up expectations for Federal Reserve interest rate hikes. The currency's strength followed a strong jobs report that reinforced the case for tighter monetary policy to combat persistent inflation.

The dollar's rally affected currencies across Asia and Europe, with regional foreign exchange markets adjusting to the shift in Fed pricing. Analysts noted that the combination of strong employment data and the dollar's surge has created new pressures for central banks outside the United States.

cards.headline: Nvidia signs multi-year chip development partnership with SK Hynix
cards.teaser: The chipmaker secured agreements with South Korean technology companies to advance artificial intelligence infrastructure and processor development.
cards.body:
Nvidia announced a multi-year agreement with SK Hynix to develop artificial intelligence chips, expanding its partnerships with South Korean technology giants. The deal includes collaboration on AI infrastructure and represents a deepening of ties between the American chip designer and Korean manufacturers.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said the company's new Vera chip will incorporate SK Hynix memory chips, highlighting the integrated nature of the partnership. The agreement also extends to other Korean firms including NAVER, which is expanding its AI infrastructure using Nvidia technology to meet growing global demand for artificial intelligence capabilities.

hero.headline: Astronomers identify source of repeating cosmic radio signals
hero.body:
Astronomers have identified the source of mysterious repeating radio signals from space, solving a puzzle that has intrigued scientists for years. A student astronomer helped pinpoint the signals to an accreting white dwarf binary system, providing what researchers are calling a Rosetta stone for understanding these cosmic phenomena.

The periodic radio and X-ray emissions come from a binary star system where a white dwarf pulls material from a companion star. This discovery, published in Nature, marks the first time scientists have definitively traced these specific types of repeating signals to their origin. The white dwarf system produces both radio waves and X-rays in a predictable pattern, allowing researchers to study the mechanics of these stellar interactions in unprecedented detail.

Researchers at UNC-Chapel Hill contributed to cracking the cosmic radio mystery by analyzing the signal patterns and comparing them with known astronomical phenomena. The repeating nature of the signals initially puzzled scientists because they arrived at regular intervals, leading to speculation about their source. The breakthrough came when astronomers were able to match the radio emissions with corresponding X-ray data from the same location in space.

The identification of this white dwarf binary as the source helps explain how matter behaves under extreme gravitational conditions. As material from the companion star spirals onto the white dwarf, it heats up and releases energy across multiple wavelengths. The regular timing of the signals corresponds to the orbital period of the binary system, creating a natural clock that astronomers can use to study stellar physics.

This discovery provides scientists with a new tool for understanding similar signals detected elsewhere in the universe. The white dwarf binary serves as a template for identifying other systems that may be producing comparable emissions. Researchers plan to use these findings to search for additional examples and to refine models of how matter accretes onto dense stellar remnants.

cards.headline: Microsoft unveils Surface Laptop Ultra at Computex
cards.teaser: Microsoft demonstrated its new Surface Laptop Ultra at the Computex technology conference, alongside announcements from Nvidia about AI-powered personal computing hardware.
cards.body:
Microsoft showed its Surface Laptop Ultra at Computex, signaling a push into high-performance personal computing. The device was available for hands-on demonstrations at the conference, where attendees could test the new hardware firsthand.

Nvidia announced its RTX Spark chip at the same event, which the company describes as its most efficient PC processor to date. Nvidia and Microsoft framed their announcements around personal AI computing, with new hardware designed to run AI applications locally on Windows PCs. The RTX Spark chip and accompanying N1x and N1 laptop processors represent Nvidia's effort to bring AI processing capabilities to consumer laptops.

cards.headline: Apple prepares updated Siri with AI features at WWDC
cards.teaser: Apple is set to announce updates to Siri and other AI features at its Worldwide Developers Conference, two years after earlier efforts to integrate artificial intelligence fell short.
cards.body:
Apple will hold its WWDC 2026 keynote, where the company is expected to unveil a revamped version of Siri powered by Google's Gemini technology. The announcement comes after two years of setbacks in Apple's AI development efforts. The company is positioning this event as a chance to reset its artificial intelligence strategy.

The conference will also include previews of iOS 27 and macOS 27, along with other software updates across Apple's product line. Observers view the event as particularly important for Apple, which has lagged behind competitors in rolling out AI features. The integration of Gemini represents a shift in Apple's approach to developing its voice assistant technology.

cards.headline: Diver films rare Great White shark in Mediterranean
cards.teaser: A volunteer diver captured footage of an endangered Great White shark swimming between Tunisia and Sicily, documenting one of the rare sightings of the species in the Mediterranean.
cards.body:
A volunteer diver documented a rare encounter with an endangered Great White shark in the Mediterranean Sea between Tunisia and Sicily. The diver reported feeling nervous while recording the footage of the marine animal.

The sighting is significant because Great White sharks are rarely seen in Mediterranean waters. The video provides important documentation of the species' presence in the region.

cards.headline: Valheim sets September release date for version 1.0
cards.teaser: The survival game Valheim will launch its full 1.0 release on September 9, adding the Deep North biome as the final major content update.
cards.body:
Developer Iron Gate Studio announced that Valheim will exit early access on September 9 with version 1.0. The update introduces the Deep North biome, a treacherous icy region serving as the game's final area. The release marks the completion of the game's planned content roadmap.

Valheim will also launch on Nintendo Switch 2 on the same day, with a new trailer showcasing the port. The game has been in early access since its initial launch, during which the developers expanded the player base while adding content and refining gameplay systems.

cards.headline: Sega addresses AI content in Crazy Taxi reboot
cards.teaser: Sega confirmed that generative AI was used in development of Crazy Taxi World Tour and responded to questions about the technology's role in the game.
cards.body:
Sega has confirmed its use of generative AI in developing Crazy Taxi World Tour, the upcoming 2027 reboot of the classic 1999 arcade game. The acknowledgment came after observers questioned the technology's involvement in the project.

The new game will feature the franchise's original punk rock soundtrack and maintain the core gameplay that defined the series. Crazy Taxi World Tour launches on Xbox and other platforms in 2027.

cards.headline: Atlus announces Persona 6 at Xbox Games Showcase
cards.teaser: Atlus officially announced Persona 6 during the Xbox Games Showcase, revealing the next entry in the role-playing game series.
cards.body:
Atlus confirmed Persona 6 during the Xbox Games Showcase at Summer Game Fest 2026, marking the official announcement of the next entry in the long-running RPG series. The announcement came as a brief teaser with limited details about the game's direction or features.

The reveal was part of a strong showing for Japanese RPGs at this year's Summer Game Fest, which also featured the announcement of the Final Fantasy VII remake trilogy's conclusion.

hero.headline: Nelly Korda wins US Women's Open for first time
hero.body:
Nelly Kord claimed her first US Women's Open title on Sunday, holding off England's Charley Hull and Mexico's Gaby Lopez by a single stroke. The world number one secured the victory with a dramatic final putt on the 18th green that caught the edge of the cup and dropped in after touring nearly half the circumference of the hole.

Kord's winning round included a steady two-under 69 in the final day of competition. The decisive moment came on the 18th hole, where her second putt from just over two feet took an unlikely path before falling into the cup to seal the championship.

This US Women's Open victory marks Kord's fourth major championship overall and her second consecutive major win. The triumph fulfills a childhood dream for the American golfer, who has become the dominant force in women's professional golf this season.

Hull mounted a strong challenge throughout the final round but ultimately fell just short of capturing her first major title. The English golfer's runner-up finish represents her best result at a major championship to date. Lopez also finished one stroke behind, sharing second place with Hull.

Kord's performance during the tournament demonstrated the consistency and skill that have established her as the world's top-ranked player. Her ability to perform under pressure in crucial moments proved decisive in separating her from a competitive field.

The victory at the US Women's Open adds to Kord's impressive resume and reinforces her position as women's golf's leading player. Her win continues what has been a dominant season at the highest level of professional women's golf, showcasing her exceptional talent across major championships.

Kord claimed the $2.5 million first prize for her victory, further cementing her status as one of the sport's elite competitors. Her success comes after building momentum from her previous major championship win, which carried into this tournament as she fought her way to the top of the leaderboard.

The narrow one-shot margin reflected the competitive nature of the championship, with multiple players positioned to challenge for the title entering the final holes. Kord's composure and execution when it mattered most ultimately separated her from the rest of the field.

This maiden US Women's Open title represents a significant career milestone for Kord, who has established herself as a major championship winner. Her performance throughout the event showcased the mental toughness and technical skill required to compete at golf's highest level and emerge victorious in close competitions.

cards.headline: Alexander Zverev wins French Open for first Grand Slam title
cards.teaser: Alexander Zverev captured his first Grand Slam championship with a five-set victory at the French Open.
cards.body:
Alexander Zverev claimed his first Grand Slam title at the French Open, defeating Italian Flavio Cobolli 6-1, 4-6, 6-4, 6-7 (5), 6-1 in the final. The second-seeded German's emotional victory came in his fourth major final appearance after three previous losses at Grand Slams.

Zverev had achieved success across tennis at every level except the majors, winning Masters 1000 events, two ATP Finals titles, and an Olympic gold medal. When Cobolli missed an overhead on the second championship point, Zverev collapsed to his back in tears, releasing years of tension from his pursuit of a Grand Slam crown.

cards.headline: Jose Mourinho to become Real Madrid head coach
cards.teaser: Jose Mourinho is set to be confirmed as Real Madrid's new head coach following Florentino Perez's re-election as club president.
cards.body:
Jose Mourinho will be confirmed as Real Madrid's new head coach following Florentino Perez's re-election as club president until 2030. Perez secured victory with 65% of the vote in the club's first competitive election in 20 years, defeating challenger Enrique Riquelme.

Real Madrid will pay Benfica a €15 million release fee to bring the Portuguese coach to the Bernabéu. Mourinho's appointment was contingent on Perez's election victory, which removes the final obstacle to his formal announcement as manager.

cards.headline: Denny Hamlin wins at Michigan for third victory of season
cards.teaser: Denny Hamlin captured his third NASCAR victory of 2026 at Michigan International Speedway.
cards.body:
Denny Hamlin won the NASCAR Cup Series race at Michigan International Speedway, claiming his third victory of the 2026 season. The race was interrupted by a red flag following a crash involving Christopher Bell and Chase Elliott that damaged the track wall.

Hamlin dedicated the win to Kyle Busch after crossing the finish line. The victory came after he navigated the race stoppage and held off competitors to secure the checkered flag at the Michigan track.

cards.headline: Christian Eriksen in good spirits after collapse, set for hospital discharge
cards.teaser: Denmark midfielder Christian Eriksen is expected to be discharged from hospital soon after collapsing during a match against Ukraine.
cards.body:
Christian Eriksen is recovering well following his collapse during Denmark's Euro 2020 match against Ukraine. According to Denmark's national team doctor Morten Boesen, the midfielder is in good spirits as he prepares to leave the hospital.

The positive update provides reassurance following the alarming incident that occurred during the international fixture, when Eriksen received immediate medical attention on the pitch.

cards.headline: Rugby league team suffers record 134-0 defeat
cards.teaser: The Crusaders lost 134-0 in the biggest defeat by any side in the top two divisions in rugby league's 131-year history.
cards.body:
The Crusaders have suffered the worst defeat in rugby league history, losing 134-0 to their opponents. This scoreline represents the largest margin of defeat ever recorded by any team competing in the top two divisions of the sport across its 131-year history.

The result stands as an unprecedented outcome in professional rugby league competition, surpassing all previous records for the heaviest loss at the highest levels of the game.

cards.headline: Alabama baseball game with St. Johns moved to later start time
cards.teaser: Alabama's Super Regional matchup with St. Johns has been pushed to a later start time after weather delays.
cards.body:
The Alabama baseball team's Super Regional game against St. Johns was moved to a later start time. The adjustment came after weather conditions interrupted the series in Tuscaloosa.

Alabama holds a lead in the series and was six outs away from advancing to Omaha when play was suspended. The game is set to resume with the Crimson Tide looking to close out the victory and secure their spot in the College World Series.

hero.headline: Qween Jean becomes first openly trans person to win Tony Award
hero.body:
Costume designer Qween Jean made history at the Tony Awards as the first openly trans person to win the prestigious award. Jean won recognition for her costume design work on the musical Cats, marking a significant milestone for transgender representation in theater's most prominent awards ceremony.

During her acceptance speech, Jean addressed the broader cultural moment and societal challenges facing the nation. "The world right now is deeply, deeply combating so many ailments, and we know as a society that when we come together, we can make real, permanent change," she said to the audience.

The Tony Awards ceremony took place at Radio City Music Hall and featured several historic achievements across multiple categories. The evening opened with a large-scale production number featuring the song Lady Marmalade, with dozens of performers promoting themes of unity and celebration.

Jean's work on Cats involved creating distinctive costume designs to bring the feline characters to life on stage. The musical, based on T.S. Eliot's Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats with music by Andrew Lloyd Webber, has remained a staple of theatrical production since its original 1981 premiere. The costume design for the current production competed among other notable entries in the technical categories.

Jean's historic win came alongside other significant achievements throughout the evening. Actor John Lithgow set a record as the oldest male performer to win a competitive acting Tony at age 80 for his role in Giant. This broke a previous record that had stood since 2000.

The revival of Arthur Miller's Death of a Salesman emerged as the night's biggest winner overall, taking home six awards across various categories. The musical Schmigadoon! won the award for best musical, continuing the night's theme of celebrating theatrical excellence and innovation.

The ceremony emphasized inclusivity and cultural recognition, with the opening production number setting the tone for an evening dedicated to honoring theatrical achievement. Jean's historic recognition as the first openly trans Tony winner represents an important moment for representation in one of theater's most visible and celebrated events.

Her win comes at a time of heightened national conversation surrounding transgender rights, visibility, and representation across various sectors of society and culture. The Tony Awards have long served as a major platform for recognizing excellence in theater while also reflecting broader conversations about diversity and inclusion in the arts.

cards.headline: John Lithgow wins Tony at 80, becomes oldest male acting winner
cards.teaser: The actor set a record for oldest man to win a competitive acting Tony, breaking a mark held since 2000.
cards.body:
John Lithgow made Tony Award history at age 80, winning actor in a play for his role in Giant. He surpassed Roy Dotrice's previous record as the oldest man to win a competitive acting Tony. Dotrice held the distinction since 2000 when he won featured actor in a play for A Moon for the Misbegotten at age 77.

This marks Lithgow's third Tony Award, spanning three of the four acting categories across a 53-year career. His first Tony came in 1973. A revival of Arthur Miller's Death of a Salesman dominated the evening with six awards total.

cards.headline: Death of a Salesman revival leads Tony Awards with six wins
cards.teaser: The Arthur Miller play took home the most awards at the 79th annual ceremony.
cards.body:
A revival of Arthur Miller's Death of a Salesman won six Tony Awards, making it the biggest winner of the night. The production earned recognition across multiple categories at the ceremony held at Radio City Music Hall.

Lesley Manville was among the winners from the production, sharing top honors with John Lithgow who won for a different play. The revival brought renewed attention to Miller's 1949 drama about an aging salesman confronting the failures of his American Dream.

cards.headline: Scary Movie reboot opens atop box office with $105 million globally
cards.teaser: The horror comedy parody earned $55 million domestically in its opening weekend.
cards.body:
The new Scary Movie film claimed the top spot at the domestic box office with a $55 million opening weekend, bringing its global total to $105 million. The R-rated comedy parody surpassed Masters of the Universe, which opened in second place the same weekend.

The sixth installment of the franchise marks a return for the parody series, which has built its reputation on timing and cultural relevance. The film's strong performance continues a recent trend of low-budget films finding box office success.

cards.headline: Pink hosts Tony Awards with Lady Marmalade performance featuring Megan Thee Stallion
cards.teaser: The opening number packed the stage with dozens of performers including Neil Patrick Harris.
cards.body:
Pink opened the 2026 Tony Awards with a Broadway-scale rendition of "Lady Marmalade" from Moulin Rouge. The performance brought together an ensemble of performers including Megan Thee Stallion, Neil Patrick Harris, Lea Michele, Dylan Mulvaney, June Squibb, and Shoshana Bean.

The 79th Tony Awards ceremony at Radio City Music Hall celebrated theatrical achievement across multiple categories. Schmigadoon! won Best Musical, while Death of a Salesman earned significant recognition with wins for John Lithgow and Lesley Manville.

cards.headline: Schmigadoon! wins best musical at Tony Awards
cards.teaser: The musical took home the top prize on Broadway's biggest night.
cards.body:
The musical Schmigadoon! won best musical at the 2026 Tony Awards. Death of a Salesman emerged as the night's biggest winner with multiple awards, while acting honors went to John Lithgow, Laurie Metcalf, Joshua Henry, and Lesley Manville across various categories.

At 80 years old, Lithgow made Tony history as the oldest male actor to win a competitive acting award for his role in Giant, breaking a 53-year-old record.

cards.headline: The Vampire Lestat premieres with new narrator perspective
cards.teaser: The third season of Interview With The Vampire shifts focus to Lestat's version of events.
cards.body:
The premiere episode of The Vampire Lestat aired, introducing a new narrative perspective centered on the title character. Sam Reid plays a dual role in the production, which represents a shift from previous seasons that focused on Louis's narration.

The episode introduces the character Gabriella as part of the expanded story. The series enters what producers describe as a vibrant Vampire Lestat era, contrasting with earlier seasons. Critics noted the show continues to build on its established quality while exploring new narrative territory.

hero.headline: Trump's intelligence pick scuttles bipartisan deal on surveillance powers
hero.body:
President Trump's decision to appoint Bill Pulte as director of national intelligence has derailed congressional efforts to secure a long-term extension of Section 702 surveillance authorities. The move has upended what appeared to be a bipartisan agreement on renewing the controversial spy powers.

Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act allows intelligence agencies to collect communications of foreign targets operating outside the country without a warrant. The provision has sparked intense debate between national security officials who argue it remains essential for counterterrorism operations and civil liberties advocates concerned about potential government overreach.

A procedural vote in the Senate on Friday underscored the political damage caused by Pulte's appointment. Seven Republican senators joined all Democrats to block the extension measure in a 47-52 vote. Senate Majority Leader John Thune acknowledged the chamber would attempt another vote the following week but expressed limited confidence it would succeed.

Pulte, a major Republican donor and heir to a home construction fortune, has no previous experience in intelligence work. He currently leads the Federal Housing Finance Agency and has overseen Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. Democrats and some Republicans have raised serious concerns about his appointment. Mark Warner, the Senate Intelligence Committee vice-chair, told NPR that Pulte was selected solely for his loyalty to Trump and that his lack of intelligence, law enforcement, or congressional experience would essentially "disarm" the country against adversaries including Russia, China, and Iran.

Warner personally asked Senate leadership to convince Trump to reverse the appointment, with Democratic sources indicating that a bipartisan surveillance deal could collapse without such intervention. Republican concerns also centered on Trump's use of Pulte to challenge Trump's political opponents, with Senator Thune warning that a "weaponized" national intelligence director would face significant obstacles to permanent confirmation.

Trump has compounded these concerns by instructing Pulte to begin firing personnel at the intelligence office. Speaking to the Wall Street Journal, Trump said the director of national intelligence position is "unnecessary and/or too big" and wants it reduced. He told Pulte he is "less shackled" in his temporary role, suggesting this status gives him more power to take drastic action during his limited time in the position.

The surveillance program is set to expire next week. An earlier attempt to extend Section 702 for 18 months failed in the House last month after 20 Republican representatives rebelled against the measure, leading to a compromise 45-day negotiation period.

The uncertainty surrounding Section 702's future comes as Trump has also suggested using his intelligence apparatus to investigate unsubstantiated claims about election fraud, raising additional questions about the direction of the intelligence community under his administration.

cards.headline: Trump walks out of interview when pressed on election fraud claims
cards.teaser: The president ended an interview on Meet the Press after repeated questions about his claims regarding the 2020 election and recent California primaries.
cards.body:
President Trump abruptly ended an NBC Meet the Press interview after clashing with host Kristen Welker over his election claims. The interview was conducted Friday in Wisconsin and aired Sunday.

Welker repeatedly challenged Trump on his assertions that the 2020 presidential election was rigged and questioned him about compensation for those charged in the January 6 insurrection. Rather than continue the exchange, Trump walked out of the interview.

cards.headline: Treasury plans to use Iranian assets for Gulf reconstruction
cards.teaser: The Treasury Department intends to redirect frozen Iranian assets to help Gulf allies rebuild damage from the war, according to a report citing sources familiar with the secretary's thinking.
cards.body:
The Treasury Department plans to use Iranian assets to assist Gulf allies in rebuilding after damage sustained during the war with Iran, CBS News reported. A source aware of Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's thinking said the department intends to redirect the frozen assets for reconstruction efforts in Gulf nations.

The move would represent a significant use of Iranian financial holdings to compensate countries affected by Iranian military actions. The United States has maintained frozen Iranian assets for years, and their potential use for allied reconstruction marks a shift in how those funds might be deployed.

cards.headline: Bass and Raman advance to Los Angeles mayoral runoff
cards.teaser: Mayor Karen Bass and City Council member Nithya Raman will face off in November to lead the nation's second-largest city.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass and City Council member Nithya Raman are projected to advance to the November general election for mayor of Los Angeles. With 87 percent of votes counted, Bass leads with 34.68 percent while Raman has 27.12 percent from the primary held on June 2.

The two Democrats will compete to lead the country's second-largest city. Bass currently serves as mayor, while Raman represents a City Council district. The November election will determine who guides Los Angeles through ongoing challenges including homelessness, public safety, and urban development.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins Democratic primary for New Mexico governor
cards.teaser: The former Biden administration official could become the first female Native American governor if elected in November.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico. The former Biden administration official secured the nomination to run in the general election this fall.

Haaland could make history as the first female Native American governor if she wins in November. She previously served in the Biden administration and has been a prominent figure in Democratic politics, bringing both executive branch experience and a focus on Native American issues to her gubernatorial campaign.

cards.headline: California governor primary narrows to frontrunners from both parties
cards.teaser: Steve Hilton and Xavier Becerra lead the crowded field seeking to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra are leading California's gubernatorial primary to replace Governor Gavin Newsom. Democrats Katie Porter and Tom Steyer, along with Republican Chad Bianco, are also competing in the race.

California's top-two primary system advances the two candidates with the most votes to the general election regardless of party affiliation. Current results show the frontrunners represent different parties, setting up a cross-party matchup for November.

cards.headline: Former Oregon senator Bob Packwood dies at 93
cards.teaser: Packwood resigned from the Senate in 1995 after the Ethics Committee voted to expel him for sexual and official misconduct.
cards.body: Former US senator Bob Packwood of Oregon has died at age 93. The moderate Republican, who was known as an advocate for abortion rights and women's issues, resigned from the Senate in 1995 following allegations of sexual harassment. The Senate Ethics Committee had voted to expel him for sexual and official misconduct, making him one of the few senators in modern history to face such action. His family announced his death on Saturday.
